nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM k-CUT accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when decoding $x$ with the canonical bitstring encoding of instances of MAXIMUM k-CUT succeeds and yields an instance that is well formed and feasible. All other bitstrings, including those that fail to decode, are rejected.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM k-CUT as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, k, K)$ of MAXIMUM k-CUT is feasible when there are a list $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of $n$ natural numbers, each less than $k$, and a list $C$ of length at least $K$ obtained from $E$ by deleting zero or more of its entries, such that $a_u \ne a_v$ for every pair $(u, v)$ in $C$, where $a_w$ is read as $0$ when $w \ge n$.
nodes.title: Feasible MAXIMUM k-CUT instances

nodes.summary: An instance of MAXIMUM k-CUT is a quadruple $(n, E, k, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the edges), a natural number $k$ (the number of parts) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).
nodes.title: Instances of MAXIMUM k-CUT

nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM k-CUT lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to MAXIMUM k-CUT.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM k-CUT is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E, k, K)$ of MAXIMUM k-CUT is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and the reversed pair $(v, u)$ does not occur in $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed MAXIMUM k-CUT instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
